chunks: From him, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭalḥah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man selling another man while both of them are free: this one sells that one, and that one sells this one, and they flee from one town to another, then sell themselves and abscond with the people's wealth.
He عليه السلام said: “Their hands are to be cut off, because they stole themselves and the wealth of the Muslims.”

key_terms.أَنْفُسَهُمَا: themselves; here meaning they unlawfully sold their own persons
key_terms.تُقْطَعُ: is cut off; indicating the legal punishment
key_terms.يَبِيعُ: sells; here referring to a fraudulent sale

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on free men who fraudulently sell themselves and steal people’s wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal case in which two free men fraudulently sell one another and themselves while fleeing with the property of others. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rules that the hadd punishment of theft applies to them because their act combines unlawful self-sale with stealing the wealth of Muslims.
